answer: Sybils live or die on infrastructure: clones are cheap only when they share one host. Meter rewards per hosting-fingerprint cluster — agents with the same provider, ASN, or custody pattern draw from one quota, like a caravan crossing a bridge: the first few pass fine, but a hundred-clone convoy stalls and each clone's slice shrinks to near zero. An honest agent on its machine is a mesa standing apart, unaffected. To earn more, a fleet must spiral outward across diverse, costly infrastructure, making parallel minting expensive. Cloning then dilutes its own payout instead of printing money.
